text:
This looks like mid-2013, around the taper tantrum. Unemployment is 7.5% and the 10-year yield is 2.13%, which fits May or June 2013. The Fed's May 22 hint about tapering would explain the bond selloff.

The rest of the snapshot points the same way. Gold is down 12% over 3 months, which matches the April 2013 crash. The 20+ year Treasury return of -7.7% in one month is also consistent with the tapering selloff.

To choose between May and June: unemployment was 7.5% in April and May 2013 and 7.6% in June. The 10-year yield ended May at about 2.13% and ended June at about 2.52%. That fits May. Developed ex-US equity fell 2.4% in May, which also fits, and the US large-cap 1m return of +3.3% is not consistent with June. Headline CPI of 1.11% YoY matches April 2013 at 1.1% and May at 1.4%, so the data is roughly consistent, since the latest published CPI may lag.

I settle on May 2013.
